    1. transmogrify(Function)

Schnittstelle Transmogrifyable<SELF extends Transmogrifyable<?>>

Typparameter:
SELF - the implementing type (self type)
Alle bekannten Unterschnittstellen:
Either<L,R>, Eval<A>, Maybe<A>, Provider<A>, Result<A>
Alle bekannten Implementierungsklassen:
Either.Left, Either.Right, Eval.Always, Eval.Later, Eval.Now, Maybe.None, Maybe.Some, Nothing, Record2, Record3, Record4, Result.Failure, Result.Success
Funktionsschnittstelle:
Dies ist eine funktionale Schnittstelle, die somit als Zuweisungsziel für einen Lambdaausdruck oder eine Methodenreferenz verwendet werden kann.
@FunctionalInterface public interface Transmogrifyable<SELF extends Transmogrifyable<?>>

Interface for types that can be transformed (“transmogrified”) into another type via a user‑provided function. This enables fluent conversion pipelines without coupling to a specific target type.

Sometimes it’s convenient to “transform” an object into a different representation and keep working fluently with the result. Implementing Transmogrifyable provides a single, explicit hook for such conversions.

Pop‑culture footnote: The term “Transmogrifier” pays homage to Calvin & Hobbes’ cardboard box invention (see Calvin & Hobbes, 1987‑03‑23). Variants of the idea also pop up across classic sci‑fi (Star Trek, anyone?).

  • Methodendetails

    • transmogrify

      <T> @NonNull T transmogrify(@NonNull Function<? super SELF, ? extends T> transmogrifier)

      Applies the given transformation to this instance and returns the result, enabling fluent conversion to an arbitrary target type.

      Contract: transmogrifier must not be null and must not return null.

      Typparameter:
      T - the target type produced by the transformation
      Parameter:
      transmogrifier - the transformation function; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      a non‑null value of type T
